title: Problem 1.1 (Bucić–Letzter–Sudakov)
statement_text: Is it true that $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H) = O_\Delta(n)$ for every acyclic digraph $H$ with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$?
context_text: This is the directed analogue of the classical Burr–Erdős conjecture. Bucić, Letzter, and Sudakov posed it after proving that oriented Ramsey numbers of bounded-degree oriented trees are linear in the number of vertices. The present paper is centrally devoted to answering it.
paper_contribution: Disproves the problem by constructing, for any $\Delta \geq 2$ and $n$ sufficiently large, an acyclic digraph $H$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfying $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H) \geq n^{\Omega(\Delta^{2/3}/\log^{5/3}\Delta)}$, showing that $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)$ is not always linear in $n$ for bounded-degree acyclic digraphs.
notes: PDF source; statement is simple and reads cleanly.

title: Open problem on parameters governing $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)$
statement_text: What natural parameters (analogous to degeneracy and vertex count for undirected graphs) determine the growth order of $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)$ for acyclic digraphs? In particular, is $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)$ polynomial or super-polynomial in $n$ when $H$ has bounded degree?
context_text: Digraphs are simple and oriented (no loops, parallel or anti-parallel edges). For an acyclic digraph $H$, the oriented Ramsey number $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)$ is the least $N$ such that every tournament on $N$ vertices contains a copy of $H$ (more generally $\overrightarrow{r}_k(H)$ asks for a monochromatic copy in every $k$-edge-coloured tournament; acyclicity is needed since transitive tournaments contain no directed cycle); $n$ denotes the number of vertices and $\Delta$ the maximum degree of $H$. For undirected graphs, the Burr–Erdős conjecture (bounded-degeneracy graphs have linear Ramsey number) was proved by Lee, and the degeneracy $d$ and the number $n$ of vertices essentially govern $r_2(H)$: $r_2(H)\ge\max(n,2^{d/2})$, and Conlon, Fox and Sudakov conjectured $r_2(H)=2^{O(d)}n$ (known up to a $\log^2d$ factor in the exponent). Disproving the directed analogue of Burr–Erdős (a question of Bucić, Letzter and Sudakov), the authors construct, for every $\Delta\ge2$ and large $n$, acyclic $H$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)\ge n^{\Omega(\Delta^{2/3}/\log^{5/3}\Delta)}$, while the worst case is at most $2^{O(\Delta\log^2(2n/\Delta))}$; typical bounded-degree acyclic digraphs have nearly linear oriented Ramsey number, and for $k\ge2$ colours there are acyclic $H$ of maximum degree 3 with $\overrightarrow{r}_k(H)\ge n^{\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)}$. They identify multiscale complexity as a relevant parameter: order $V(H)$ so that all edges go forward (a topological sorting), give each edge $v_i\to v_j$ the length $j-i$, and say $H$ has high multiscale complexity if for most dyadic scales $[2^t,2^{t+1})$ many edges have length in that scale; their upper bounds are stronger for low complexity, and their lower-bound digraphs (interval meshes) maximize it. They conjecture that super-polynomial growth $\overrightarrow{r}_1(H)\ge n^{\omega(1)}$ occurs already for one colour and some fixed $\Delta$.
notes: Stated as prose in the introduction (no formal theorem environment); also reiterated in the conclusion.
